extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, license applicants, search-and-rescue organizations, and other stakeholders seeking to build, certify, license, operate, or comment on PELTS (Personal Emergency Locator Transmitter Service) systems
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and technical specifications for establishing and operating the Personal Emergency Locator Transmitter Service (PELTS), including eligibility, licensing, equipment type-acceptance, frequency/channel allocations, emission and power limits, operator duties, and location/antenna restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and Scope of PELTS
rubrics_metrics.description: This Notice proposes to establish a new radio service to provide individuals in remote areas a means to alert others of distress situations and to assist search and rescue personnel in locating those in distress; intended primarily for short-distance personal and emergency communications in isolated areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the objective: provide personal emergency communications and alerting capabilities in remote areas; emphasizes safety-of-life use and that technical parameters are set forth in subpart E (and Subpart F establishes regulatory framework).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Base Station Licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Licenses for PELTS base stations will only be granted to governmental entities or private organizations recognized by governmental entities to perform search and rescue functions; licenses will not be granted to a foreign government or a representative of a foreign government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical licensees expected include sheriff departments, state or federal park services, and ski resorts; mobile station use is not limited (mobile eligibility not restricted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing Requirement and Authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity must obtain a license from the Commission prior to operating a PELTS base station; no individual license is required for PELTS mobile stations—mobile use is authorized under the base station license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications use FCC Form 574 (new station) and must be submitted to FCC Attention: PELTS, Gettysburg, PA; defective applications (incomplete form, missing information, or missing certifications) will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Contents / Required Basic Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for a new or modified base station license must include: applicant’s name and U.S. mailing address; station class; number of base stations and mobile units; each base station location (latitude/longitude within one second and street address or local directions); antenna height and ground elevation; area of operation; applicant’s signature; transmitting channels requested; transmitter power; ERP; emission designator; primary control point and telephone number; eligibility statement; copy of governmental recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All items (§95.723 (a)-(o)) are required; missing required information renders an application defective and subject to return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Signature and Authorized Signatory
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant is an individual, the individual must sign; if other entity types, specified individuals must sign (e.g., partner for partnership, an officer for associations/governmental units).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatory rules identify who may sign depending on entity type (see §95.725).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Processing, Grants, and Rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may grant an application in part or subject to conditions without a hearing; the applicant is presumed to have accepted a conditioned grant unless a written rejection is filed within 30 days of the grant or its effective date; notice of rejection triggers vacatur and a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should monitor grant notices and timely file rejection if not accepting conditions; incomplete applications are returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: License Term and Renewal Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A base station license is usually issued for a 5-year term; renewal applications use FCC Form 574-R (or Form 405-A if Form 574-R not received within 30 days of expiration) and must be timely filed before expiration to continue operating pending grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If renewal application is timely filed before expiration, base station may continue to operate under the expired license until FCC action; keep a copy of the renewal application with station records until action received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification, Notification, and Transfer of License
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes requiring a license modification application (Form 574) before operating under new parameters include change in frequency, power, antenna height, station location, number of mobile units, or change in corporate ownership/control; changes in mailing address or name only require notification by letter to FCC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee may not operate under new parameters until FCC approves modification; transfer/assignment of a base station license is prohibited except with prior Commission approval for corporate control changes (consent requested via FCC Form 703).

rubrics_metrics.name: Station Recordkeeping Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PELTS base station licensees must maintain station records for the license term, including: the license; copies of letters from the licensee to the FCC concerning name or mailing address changes; copies of answers to discrepancy notices; an STA or waiver of rules; copy of any renewal application submitted and not acted upon; copy of any FCC waiver to use an antenna higher than normally allowed; copy of FCC consent to corporate control change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must be retained for the license term and made available as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel Sharing and Interference Resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Channels assigned in the PELTS are available only on a shared basis and will not be assigned for the exclusive use of any licensee; all applicants and licensees shall cooperate in channel selection and use to reduce interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees suffering from or causing harmful interference are expected to cooperate and resolve problems mutually; if unable, FCC may impose restrictions (transmitter power, antenna height, area/hours of operation) or deny use in locations not in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel Uses and Permissible Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel-specific permissible uses: Channels 1,2,6,7 limited to emergency assistance voice communications involving safety of life and property; Channel 3 limited to one-way non-commercial informational voice messages (weather, hazards, closings, etc.); Channels 4,5,8,9 limited to short-distance personal voice communications; Channel 10 limited to non-voice emergency alerting/homing transmissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority must be given to (text continues) — licensees/operators must respect channel-specific use restrictions and prioritize emergency communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency Allocations and Protected Bands
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequencies 121.500 MHz and 243.000 MHz cannot be used for PELTS because they are reserved for international aviation and maritime emergency systems; the Notice proposes using the 220-222 MHz band for PELTS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 220-222 MHz band offers propagation characteristics suitable for isolated/wooded areas; use of one five-channel block (five channel pairs) is proposed for two-way voice, alerting, and homing; comments solicited on frequency choice and licensing schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Channel Frequencies and US314 Footnote
rubrics_metrics.description: The frequency bands 220.9775-220.9975 and 221.9775-221.9975 MHz are limited to Personal Emergency Locator Transmitter Service operations (US314 footnote); §95.626 lists channel frequencies and notes pairing and uses (some channels paired for full duplex; some reserved for simplex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain channels are paired for duplex operation and mobile relay (mobile-to-mobile through a base) operations are not permitted on specified frequencies; see §95.626 for channel-by-channel uses and pairing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency Tolerance Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each PELTS base transmitter must be maintained to within a frequency tolerance of ±0.0001 percent; mobile units must be maintained to within a frequency tolerance of ±0.00015 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type acceptance and manufacturing must ensure transmitters meet these tolerances in normal operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission Types and Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: For PELTS operations on emergency notification/homing channels only, emission types J3E or J2D will be authorized (§95.627(d) table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization of emission types depends on channel and purpose; follow §95.627's channel/emission mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission Bandwidth Limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum authorized bandwidth for any emission type transmitted by a PELTS transmitter is 3.6 kHz (§95.629(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmitters and modulation schemes must limit occupied bandwidth to 3.6 kHz or less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwanted Radiation Attenuation and Measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: For PELTS transmitters in 5 kHz channel assignments, emissions must be attenuated relative to the highest emission in the channel according to a schedule: (i) >1.8 kHz to ≤2.5 kHz: at least 100*(fd - 1.8) dB; (ii) >2.5 kHz to ≤5 kHz: at least 70 + 4*(fd - 2.5) dB; (iii) >5 kHz: at least 80 dB. Emission power measured in peak values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution bandwidth of measurement instrumentation: up to and including 5 kHz offset use 100 Hz RBW; >5 kHz use 10 kHz RBW; the reference 'highest emission within the channel' should be remeasured for each change in RBW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulation Standards and Overmodulation Prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Each GMRS and PELTS transmitter, except a GMRS mobile station or a PELTS mobile station transmitter with power output ≤2.5 W, must automatically prevent a greater-than-normal audio level from causing overmodulation (§95.633(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design must incorporate automatic limiting to prevent overmodulation except for low-power mobile exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio Low-Pass Filter Exemption and Digital Emissions Type Acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: A PELTS transmitter shall be exempt from the audio low-pass filter requirements provided that transmitters used for digital emissions must be type accepted with the digital modulating signal(s) specified by the manufacturer; type acceptance application must demonstrate compliance with emission limitations specified in §95.631 (§95.633(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital-modulation devices must include specified digital signal characteristics in the type-acceptance submission to show compliance with unwanted emission limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type Acceptance Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each PELTS transmitter (a transmitter that operates or is intended to operate at a station authorized in the PELTS) must be type accepted (§95.603(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type acceptance applications must include necessary information demonstrating compliance with emission limitations and other applicable technical requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum Transmitter Power Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: No PELTS base transmitter under any conditions of modulation shall exceed 100 watts output power (§95.635(d)). No PELTS mobile transmitter under any conditions of modulation shall exceed 3 watts output power (§95.635(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power ratings must be adhered to; applications must specify transmitter power and ERP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile Equipment Design, Safety, and Performance Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobiles in PELTS must: have ability to transmit on all PELTS mobile channels; have positive means of turning equipment off with guard to prevent inadvertent operation; have no sharp edges or projections; provide means to fasten to a person; be battery-powered with battery contained within transmitter case and have visual low-battery indicator that indicates when 75% of battery useful life has expired; have operating instructions understandable by untrained personnel permanently displayed on outside; have attached warning label that channel 10 is emergency-only and effective only in areas with a watch/response system; be waterproof and float free in calm fresh water with at least upper 10 cm out of water; have visible or audible indicator showing device is operating protected from damage; meet these requirements after free falls 3 times from 18 meters (60 feet) (§95.653(b)(1)-(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers must design mobiles to meet ruggedness, user-safety, usability, and survivability requirements; ensure labeling and instructions are permanent and clearly visible; include low-battery and operation indicators; test devices for drop survivability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel 10 Specific Warning and Use Limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile equipment must have an attached warning label clearly stating that channel 10 is to be used only for emergency alerting and is effective only in areas where there is a watch/response system in place (§95.653(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User-facing warnings must be prominent and permanent; equipment should prevent inadvertent non-emergency use of channel 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Servicing, Maintenance, and Test Transmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee responsible for proper operation and expected to provide observations, servicing and maintenance as necessary; adjustments/tests during installation/servicing/maintenance should be performed by or under immediate supervision of a person certified as technically qualified by an organization representative of users; test signals during internal adjustments should use a non-radiating simulated antenna except brief radiating test signals (no longer than 1 minute during any five-minute period) to adjust antenna or measure spurious radiation; such tests must not interfere with in-progress communications and must be properly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance procedures must minimize radiated interference; ensure qualified personnel perform tests; document test activities as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antenna Height Limits and Aircraft Safety
rubrics_metrics.description: A base station antenna must not be a hazard to aircraft; licensee must obtain FCC permission before uppermost tip exceeds permitted heights; minimum allowed height is at least 6.1 meters (20 feet) above ground or equal to existing antenna height; antenna may be as high as 61 meters (200 feet) above ground unless within 6.1 kilometers of an airport or heliport; specific slope-height limits apply when near airports/heliports (formulas based on distance and runway/pad length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If permission granted for greater height, licensee may be required to mark and light the antenna per part 17; consult FAA and FCC procedures before applying for greater heights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Requesting Antenna Height Exceedance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant seeking permission for antenna higher than normally allowed must request on FCC Form 574 and notify the Federal Aviation Administration on FAA Form 7460-1 (referred to here as 7466-1 in the text) that the antenna would be higher than normally allowed (§95.753).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required forms and FAA notification with application; failure to follow procedure may delay or deny approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation Near FCC Monitoring Stations
rubrics_metrics.description: FCC may impose additional restrictions on a PELTS base station located within 4.8 kilometers (3 miles) of an FCC monitoring station if transmissions degrade, obstruct, or repeatedly interrupt monitoring station operation; consult Chief, Field Operations Bureau before applying for such a location or modifying existing operation (§95.741).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-application consultation recommended for sites near monitoring stations to avoid operational restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Quiet Zone Notification Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants seeking to operate in the National Quiet Zone must send notice of intent to the Director, National Radio Astronomy Observatory and provide details about proposed station: antenna point (lat/long), antenna height, antenna directivity, transmitting channels, emission, and transmitter output; include the date the notice was sent to the Observatory in the FCC application (§95.743).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Quiet Zone is geographically defined; include required details and date of notice in FCC filing to comply with coordination/notification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Assessment Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for new or modified license that may have a significant effect on the environment as defined in §1.1307 must be accompanied by an Environmental Assessment (see §1.1311); environmental requirements also govern construction prior to Commission authorization (see §1.1312) (§95.745).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must evaluate environmental impacts and file EA when required; follow §§1.1307, 1.1311, and 1.1312 for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation Near International Borders
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States and the Government of Canada coordinate channel assignments to certain radio stations in border areas north of Line A and east of Line C; see §1.955 for coordination procedures (§95.747).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants near Canadian border must comply with international coordination rules and may need additional coordination steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Area of Operation (Geographic Scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are authorized to operate your PELTS station within or over any area of the world where radio services are regulated by the FCC (fifty U.S. States, DC, Puerto Rico, certain insular areas and possessions); operation is not authorized in areas where radio services are regulated by another U.S. agency or any foreign government; operation on aircraft or ship permitted with captain's permission and must follow applicable treaties (§95.749).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm territorial regulation jurisdiction before operation; if operating internationally or on transport vessels, ensure treaty obligations and permissions are observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling and User Instructions Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile units must have operating instructions understandable by untrained personnel permanently displayed on the outside and an attached warning label about channel 10 emergency use; GMRS and PELTS base station transmitter warnings must include licensing requirements and information concerning license application procedures (§95.653(b)(4); §95.649(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers and licensees must ensure user-facing materials are permanent, clear, and informative regarding licensing and emergency-channel use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and Test Instrumentation Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When measuring unwanted emissions for PELTS transmitters: emission power measured in peak values; resolution bandwidth for measuring emissions up to and including 5 kHz from center: 100 Hz; for emissions >5 kHz from center: 10 kHz; the reference highest emission within the channel should be remeasured for each change in resolution bandwidth (§95.631(b)(10)(iv)-(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test labs and manufacturers must follow specified RBW and measurement conventions to demonstrate compliance with attenuation schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex Parte and Rulemaking Comment Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a non-restricted notice-and-comment rulemaking proceeding; see §1.1206(a) for rules governing permissible ex parte contacts; comments due by March 20, 1990 and reply comments by April 19, 1990; a ninety-day comment period provided in view of Canada–U.S. Trade Agreement for proceedings affecting foreign firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders wishing to influence final rules must file timely and relevant comments and follow ex parte contact rules; international stakeholders may have extended comment period.
